payload.title: How to choose a wedding planner in Italy
payload.seo_title: Wedding Planner Italy: How to Choose One from Australia
payload.meta_description: How to choose a wedding planner in Italy from Australia: the types of planner, how Italian planners charge, the questions to ask and the red flags.
payload.excerpt: Which kind of planner your Italian wedding needs, how planners charge and who they work for, the questions that reveal a reliable one, and how to manage contracts and euro payments from Australia.
payload.author: [[NEEDS: named author]]
key_takeaways: Not every wedding in Italy needs a full planner, but a 70 to 110 guest, multi-day celebration with guests flying from Australia usually needs someone who works for you rather than for the venue.

Italian planners charge a flat fee, a percentage (often around 10% of the total wedding budget, according to Federconsumatori figures reported in June 2026) or a hybrid, so ask for a written scope, the VAT treatment and a written answer on supplier payments.
Judge a planner by a named lead, recent weddings in your region and month, references from couples who planned from overseas and a real run sheet, not by their Instagram feed.
Sydney is eight to 10 hours ahead of Italy, so agree a fixed call slot, a reply time and who will be on site on the day before you sign.

A planner can coordinate the paperwork but cannot make you married: legal validity comes from the Italian civil (or recognised religious) process, and because requirements can change, confirm the current process for your own passports.

faq.q: How much does a wedding planner in Italy cost?
faq.a: Federconsumatori figures reported in June 2026 put on-the-day coordination at about EUR 1,000 to 3,500 (about AUD 1,600 to 5,600) and full organisation from about EUR 2,500 (about AUD 4,000), rising to EUR 10,000 to 15,000 (about AUD 16,000 to 24,000) or more. Percentage fees are often around 10% of the total wedding budget. The figures include domestic weddings, and the AUD amounts use the RBA rate on 22 October 2026.

faq.q: Do we need a planner if our venue has its own wedding coordinator?
faq.a: Sometimes not. A venue coordinator works for the venue, so ask in writing whether their scope covers outside suppliers, guest transport and the run sheet. For a multi-day wedding across several places, you usually need someone working for you.

faq.q: Should we hire an Italian planner or one based in Australia?
faq.a: Either can work. An Italy-based planner brings local suppliers and the language, while an Australia-based or dual-based planner works in your hours. Choose on recent experience in your region and a named lead on the day.

faq.q: Can an Italian wedding planner make our marriage legal in Australia?
faq.a: No. Legality comes from the Italian civil (or recognised religious) process, not the planner, and Smartraveller says an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but is usually recognised if it was valid where it took place and under Australian law. Requirements can change, so a Wedded Wonderland advisor confirms the current process for your own passports before you book appointments.

faq.q: Do Italian wedding planners take commissions from suppliers?
faq.a: Ask rather than assume. Every planner should tell you in writing whether they take any payment, discount or fee from suppliers they recommend, or mark up what they supply. A disclosed arrangement can be fine; a vague reply is the warning sign.

faq.q: How far ahead should we book a wedding planner in Italy?
faq.a: Earlier is safer for peak dates. Foreign weddings in Italy cluster in May, June and July, town-hall marriage and Apostille appointments can be hard to get from May to September, and the Atto Notorio (the declaration you sign at the Italian consulate) cannot be signed more than six months before the wedding.
